datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Phoenix TECP (Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe) relative humidity (RH) sensor in situ measurements (raw DNRH and board temperature Tb; recalibrated to frost point Tf, RH, and water vapor pressure e)
datasets.instrument_sensor: Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe (TECP) RH sensor
datasets.measurement_observable: Atmospheric relative humidity (RH), frost point temperature (Tf), water vapor pressure (e); uses raw RH output (DNRH) and TECP board temperature (Tb)
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ time-series meteorology / environmental sensor measurements
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Phoenix mission sols 1–150 (Ls ~77°–148°); examples cited: sol 54 (~noon; e up to ~1.4 Pa), sol 122 (~2 a.m.; e ~0.005 Pa); in-soil campaigns on sols 46–47, 54–55, 69–71, 86, 98, 103–104, 111, 119, 122–124, 149–150
datasets.location_coverage: Phoenix landing site (68.2°N, 234.2°E); measurements in air at heights 0 to ~2.2 m (depending on robotic arm position) and near-ground (~3 cm) / ~0.8 m (noted for sols 55–56)
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Typically sampling rate 1.2 s during ~30 min blocks a few times per sol; extended blocks ~30 min to ~20 hr also taken
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Uses raw flight sensor output (DNRH) and Tb; compares to “current PDS values” from the 2016 postflight recalibration (Zent et al., 2016)
datasets.how_used: Primary dataset. The authors apply a new recalibration/translation to the Phoenix TECP RH sensor flight measurements (DNRH, Tb) to derive updated frost point (Tf), RH, and water vapor pressure (e), analyze diurnal/seasonal variability, and assess brine formation potential.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Phoenix Surface Stereo Imager (SSI) retrievals of precipitable water vapor column abundance (PWC) at the Phoenix landing site
datasets.measurement_observable: Precipitable water vapor column abundance (PWC) used to infer near-surface daytime water vapor pressure upper bounds
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Daytime retrievals; SSI measurements cited as taken between 13:00 and 17:00 LMST (per Figure 8 caption, cited from Tamppari et al., 2010)
datasets.how_used: Used as an independent surface-based constraint/comparison for daytime water vapor pressure at the Phoenix site (including setting/justifying conservative upper bounds for e and comparing seasonal maxima to the recalibrated TECP-derived values; shown in Figure 8).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM) water vapor/precipitable water column retrievals at the Phoenix landing site
datasets.instrument_sensor: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM)
datasets.measurement_observable: Water vapor column abundance / inferred water vapor pressure upper bounds at the Phoenix landing site
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Daytime; CRISM measurements cited as taken at ~14:00 LMST (per Figure 8 caption, cited from Tamppari et al., 2010)
datasets.how_used: Used as an independent orbital constraint/comparison on Phoenix-site water vapor content; supports selection of daytime upper bounds for water vapor pressure and is compared against recalibrated TECP maximum diurnal e values (Figure 8).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) data (relative humidity/meteorology) used for comparison with Phoenix
datasets.measurement_observable: Near-surface relative humidity / water vapor pressure context for day/night ratio comparison; nighttime REMS values used (~04:00–06:00)
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ time-series meteorology / environmental sensor measurements
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Nighttime window cited for ratios: ~04:00–06:00 (for Figure 9 comparison); broader REMS RH operation noted as >2,400 sols as of May 2019 (but specific sols not provided)
datasets.location_coverage: MSL landing site coordinates stated: 4.5°S, 37.4°E (Gale crater region)
datasets.how_used: Used to compare Phoenix vs. MSL near-surface water vapor behavior, including day/night water vapor pressure ratios (Figure 9) and brine stability context alongside Phoenix conditions (Figure 10).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) ChemCam passive sky spectroscopy derived water vapor pressure values (around noon)
datasets.measurement_observable: Water vapor pressure values derived from ChemCam passive sky spectroscopy (water vapor column abundance retrievals)
datasets.data_type_product_type: Derived atmospheric retrievals from passive spectroscopy
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Around noon (cited for Figure 8); used with REMS nighttime values for MSL day/night ratios (Figure 9)
datasets.how_used: Included as the MSL daytime water vapor pressure estimate (noted as supplementing unreliable daytime e from REMS) for comparisons of maximum daytime e at Phoenix vs. MSL (Figure 8) and for day/night ratio calculations at MSL (Figure 9).

queries.query: For the Phoenix lander at Mars’ northern high latitudes, I need the in situ TECP atmospheric humidity sensor time series spanning roughly the first 150 sols, using the raw humidity sensor output and electronics-board temperature to derive frost point, relative humidity, and near-surface water vapor pressure for quantifying the diurnal H2O cycle and daytime low-RH conditions.

For the Phoenix lander MECA payload, I need the calibrated/derived non-imaging datasets that include TECP environmental measurements (including humidity) together with regolith thermal/electrical property measurements acquired during robotic-arm campaigns, to evaluate atmosphere–regolith water exchange across multiple sols and compare air vs. in-soil measurement intervals.

final_output.query: For the Phoenix lander at Mars’ northern high latitudes, I need the in situ TECP atmospheric humidity sensor time series spanning roughly the first 150 sols, using the raw humidity sensor output and electronics-board temperature to derive frost point, relative humidity, and near-surface water vapor pressure for quantifying the diurnal H2O cycle and daytime low-RH conditions.

For the Phoenix lander MECA payload, I need the calibrated/derived non-imaging datasets that include TECP environmental measurements (including humidity) together with regolith thermal/electrical property measurements acquired during robotic-arm campaigns, to evaluate atmosphere–regolith water exchange across multiple sols and compare air vs. in-soil measurement intervals.

For the Phoenix lander north-polar site, I need the daytime Surface Stereo Imager–based atmospheric retrieval products that constrain column water vapor/opacity in order to place an upper bound on near-surface water vapor pressure during the warmest, driest part of the sol.

For Phoenix Surface Stereo Imager atmospheric retrievals at the landing site, I need the instrument/processing documentation necessary to understand the retrieval methodology and uncertainty sources for daytime column water-vapor constraints (e.g., acquisition geometry and calibration assumptions).

I need the MRO CRISM-derived daytime atmospheric water-vapor column products over Mars that can be used to bound near-surface water vapor pressure at the Phoenix landing site during the Phoenix operational season, focusing on mid-afternoon local time sampling and using only derived (retrieval) outputs rather than raw radiance spectra.

I need the complete PDS archive for Mars atmospheric water-vapor retrievals derived from MRO CRISM (including the associated context and documentation needed to interpret geometry, calibration assumptions, and quality screening) so I can evaluate how orbital precipitable-water constraints should be compared against in-situ humidity variability at the Phoenix landing site.

For Mars near-surface humidity studies at Gale crater, I need Curiosity REMS meteorology in physical units so I can extract predawn relative humidity (roughly 04:00–06:00 local true solar time) and compute water vapor pressure time series for day/night ratio and seasonal variability analyses.

To independently assess instrument effects and apply a custom calibration/quality-screening workflow, I need the unprocessed Curiosity REMS engineering/housekeeping and raw sensor outputs relevant to relative humidity and supporting temperatures, spanning the mission timeline at Gale crater.

Using Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity ChemCam passive sky spectroscopy acquired near local noon over Gale crater, I need radiance-calibrated spectra suitable for retrieving atmospheric water vapor column abundance and converting it to daytime water vapor pressure for comparison against other in-situ humidity constraints.

For Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity ChemCam passive sky observations taken around local noon, I need the calibrated tabular spectral products (with associated ancillary geometry/housekeeping) so I can reproduce derived daytime water vapor pressure time series and compute diurnal day-to-night contrasts when paired with nighttime meteorological humidity measurements.
